key_insight: EDA-L2D adapts when to defer AI decisions to human experts by accounting for changes in expert reliability over time.
clinical_relevance: In medical diagnosis workflows, tracking recent expert performance could improve human–AI task allocation when reliability fluctuates.
method: Models temporal shifts in expert reliability.
Conditions the deferral head on recent expert outcomes using a sequence model.
Adapts decision allocation between AI and human experts.
evidence_signal: Experiments across image classification, medical diagnosis, and hate speech detection report improved system performance versus prior L2D methods, including evaluations under irregular expert-reliability shifts.
watch_item: Deployment requires timely expert-outcome feedback; the abstract does not establish prospective clinical effectiveness.
paper_title: Learning to Defer under Expert Drift
